title: Hearing Coltrane live and in the daytime at the Jazz Workshop
summary: He heard Coltrane in 1964-66 and, while at Berklee, watched him practice at the Jazz Workshop.

story.theme_name: Playing with Coltrane and the avant-garde

blocks.x: Can you describe what that was like? Leaving the club after seeing Coltrane?

Well there was a couple of times when I left the club early and had to go outside just to kind of calm down because it was frantic, sometimes in that period we were catching him. ’64, ’65 ’66. It was just surely an eye opener and I learned, you know, the dedication. You used to watch Trane come off the bandstand and then go right into a room — either a room where they put the beer cases and all that, and he’d just keep playing. And then I was lucky enough when I was at Berklee one of my friends was a waiter at the Jazz Workshop. And he got us to go in, in the daytime we’d go in and listen to Trane practice. Because he would come to the Jazz Workshop, go into the dressing room, and then the three guys we would sit there and order a Coca Cola at lunch and there was nobody in the club and he would be practicing in the background and we’d be trying to figure out what he’s doing. And he’s right next to the bathroom so every once in a while we’d pretend we had to go to the bathroom and look in, and I remember seeing that he had a whole tableful of reeds and we used to just listen to see what he would be practicing.
